nodes.label: Backend Metric Store and cross-agent merge
nodes.norm_label: backend metric store and cross-agent merge
nodes.rationale: Counters sum, ratios recompute from summed counters (never averaged per agent), histograms merge bucket-wise. Contributions are keyed by (dimensions, agentId, the agent's own native bucketStartUtc) because keying on agentId alone let a second bucket from the same agent overwrite the first — a real bug testing caught. nodes.label: Backend Stream Processor (UBS-88)
nodes.rationale: Floors every incoming snapshot onto the backend's canonical grid using the same floor rule the agent's _bucket_start uses, applied to boundaries that may be neither phase- nor width-aligned. A bucket older than maxBucketAge is rejected as bucket_too_old and counted, never silently discarded. The wire's restarted:true is preserved per bucket per agent to drive a derived warmingUp window, avoiding an agent-side schema change.

nodes.label: M4 — Backend Ingestion, Store, Query

Averaging per-agent percentages would weight a quiet instance the same as a busy one.

nodes.label: NoLogActivity rule
nodes.rationale: absence: messages_total == 0 over 1m, critical. Structural threshold (any occurrence is an incident) and a 1m rather than 5m window to catch a dead pipeline faster.

nodes.label: M5 Rules, alerts, callbacks
nodes.rationale: Rule Engine and alert lifecycle (RE-01-04) done and tested; callback dispatch (HTTP/HMAC) not started. rules.yaml loading and SIGHUP reload are implemented but SighupRuleReloader.install() is unwired because no agent supervisor loop exists (M1).

nodes.label: Alert lifecycle FSM
nodes.rationale: inactive -> pending -> firing -> resolving -> resolved. A tier change while firing updates severity and notifies immediately, independent of renotifyInterval, without changing alertId or firstObservedUtc (FR-RUL-022). active_alert_count() counts firing/resolving only, because pending is internal bookkeeping for a condition that has not yet cleared `for` and is not yet active alert output for the maxActiveAlerts cap.

nodes.label: RuleEngine.apply_rules() hot swap
nodes.rationale: Because _states is keyed by rule NAME rather than RuleConfig object identity, a rule present in both old and new config carries its alertId/firstObservedUtc/notificationCount across a threshold change with no special-casing. A state whose rule disappeared is force-resolved with one synthetic resolved event, since a condition with no rule definition cannot legitimately stay open, rather than left frozen forever.

nodes.label: Rule Engine
nodes.rationale: A pure consumer of MA-04's MetricsSnapshot that never touches MetricsAggregator/LatencyCorrelator directly, so it is testable from hand-built snapshot fixtures. It reads whichever value the rule's source names and picks the HIGHEST tier whose condition holds. One snapshot is built per window, so evaluate() filters to rules matching that window and the caller invokes it once per window needed; gauge-sourced rules (window=None) are evaluated every call because MA-04's gauges do not vary by window.

nodes.label: Safety and suppression (silences, grace, storm cap)
nodes.norm_label: safety and suppression (silences, grace, storm cap)
nodes.rationale: Silences suppress notification while state still transitions. Startup grace (60s) blocks evaluation entirely — broader than the spec's literal 'self-health rules only', chosen as a simpler and strictly safer blanket suppression during cold start. Past maxActiveAlerts, new pending->firing transitions are suppressed and retried next tick while one AlertStorm meta-alert fires once rather than on every tick over cap. ScheduleChecker is a seam defaulting to always-active; real trading-calendar logic is separate unbuilt scope.

nodes.label: SighupRuleReloader
nodes.rationale: install() registers signal.signal(SIGHUP, ...) — the call a future agent supervisor loop makes once one exists. Nothing in the repo runs continuously yet (main.py is a stub, M1 Log Monitor unbuilt), so that wiring is untested end to end, though the loader and reload mechanism are unit-tested including a real os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGHUP) round-trip.

nodes.label: make rules-reload-demo (hot reload)
nodes.rationale: Hot reload cannot be scripted because it needs a live process to signal. It watches a TEMP COPY of config/rules.yaml so editing cannot leave the real config dirty (a drift test compares that file against DEFAULT_RULES and a stray edit would fail the suite). Four edits demonstrate: threshold raised but still matched keeps the same alertId (FR-RUL-008), raised past the observed value resolves the same alert, deleting a firing rule emits one synthetic resolved event, and a corrupt operator is rejected while the process keeps running on last-known-good rules (FR-RUL-009).

nodes.label: make rules-quickstart (17-act demo)
nodes.rationale: One FIX session's life in 17 acts across three parts; every number comes from raw FIX bytes through the real FixParser with nothing hand-stubbed, and the 14 rules are read from the live config/rules.yaml. Uses a fixed ingest clock because the rule windows are 1-15 minutes wide and on a wall clock the demo's own events would age out of their windows mid-run. Three acts declare on screen that they use a non-default config (shortened renotifyInterval, lowered maxActiveAlerts, own instance) because lowering the cap honestly beats faking a hundred concurrent alerts.

nodes.label: Event type catalogue (§2.1)
nodes.rationale: Per-type emission policy: fix.execution is SAMPLED 1:N because metrics carry the truth; parse.error is aggregated one per reason per bucket; lifecycle, rotation/truncation/stall and alert state changes are neither sampled nor rate-limited.

nodes.label: Event envelope (§2)
nodes.rationale: FR-MET-020: events are discrete, low-volume, operationally interesting records; high-volume per-message data is ONLY metrics, never events. eventId must be UUIDv7 so it is both unique and time-sortable (FR-MET-021). fields must be allowlist-only with no text/price/account/raw line and a backend validator rejecting unknown keys (FR-MET-022). Events are rate-limited per eventType per instance (default 600/min) with excess dropped and counted rather than queued, so a reject storm cannot become an event storm (FR-MET-023).

nodes.label: Alert lifecycle requirements (§2)
nodes.rationale: FR-RUL-011: dedup key is hash(ruleName + application + instanceId + sorted groupBy values); alertId is stable for one occurrence and must change for a new occurrence after resolution. FR-RUL-012: pending->firing and resolving->resolved each emit exactly one event and one callback attempt sequence. FR-RUL-013: renotify every renotifyInterval (default 30m, 0 disables) with notificationCount incremented. FR-RUL-014: state persisted in the agent state file so a restart does not duplicate notifications. FR-RUL-016: metricContext is allowlisted metrics only, never raw log lines or FIX text. FR-RUL-022: the highest matching tier wins and a tier change while firing notifies once immediately without changing alertId or firstObservedUtc.

nodes.label: Suppression and safety (§4)
nodes.rationale: FR-RUL-018: a silence suppresses notification while still recording alert state. FR-RUL-019: self-health rules are suppressed for startupGrace (60s) so a cold start pages nobody. FR-RUL-021: while NoLogActivity fires for an instance, trading rules for that instance are suppressed, since absence of data is not absence of rejects. FR-RUL-017: output is capped at maxActiveAlerts (100), beyond which one AlertStorm meta-alert is emitted and new alerts are suppressed until it drops below the cap.

nodes.label: Dependent suppression (FR-RUL-021)
nodes.rationale: While NoLogActivity is firing, every rule with depends_on_log_activity=True reads as insufficient data instead of evaluating its raw condition, because absence of data is not absence of rejects. Read once per tick from the PREVIOUS tick's state, so it lags NoLogActivity's own transition by exactly one tick — order-independent, but not same-tick.

nodes.label: HeartbeatEmitter
nodes.rationale: tick() is synchronous and pure so it can be tested one call at a time and never raises on sink failure (spec 002 §8.3: a backend outage must not affect the agent). run(stop) ticks immediately then every interval via asyncio.wait_for(stop.wait(), timeout=interval), an interruptible sleep with no busy loop. Interval is independent of log volume — that is the acceptance criterion that an idle log still heartbeats.

nodes.label: Parse error rate signal (UBS-59)
nodes.rationale: A log format change makes the parser fail on most lines and metrics quietly go to zero; someone must notice before a parsing problem is blamed on trading. Rate = errors/lines over the SAME window, because 2 errors is 100% of 2 lines and 0.02% of 10,000; zero lines yields None, not 0 and not 100%. Reason text carries numerator, denominator and window so the operator can judge confidence without a second query.

nodes.label: record_parse_result() intake
nodes.rationale: The ticket asked for a subscription to parse-error events, but there is no event bus (the pipeline bridge is M1.5), so an intake method the parser loop calls is the honest equivalent.

nodes.label: SlidingWindowCounter
nodes.rationale: Per-bucket integers keyed by bucket index, not per-event timestamps, so memory is window/bucket (300 ints) regardless of event rate — a 100k errors/s storm costs the same as an idle window. Expiry runs on every access so the count decays with no background thread. Dict-keyed-by-index rather than a deque lets a late event for a still-live second land in its bucket. Trade-off: 1s buckets mean an event can be counted up to 1s beyond exactly 300s, the same trade the Metrics Aggregator makes with 10s buckets.

nodes.label: M1.5 Pipeline bridge (UBS-48/49)
nodes.rationale: UBS-48 library done (blocking enqueue with optional drop_oldest, asymmetric queue sizing line 2048 > event 256, parser worker pool min(2, cpu_count), commit-offset-after-parse+ingest, dedupe by (dev, inode, byte_offset)); UBS-49 live integration not started, which is why nothing in production calls the Health Reporter from a parser loop.

nodes.label: telemetry-agent-heartbeat demo entrypoint
nodes.rationale: Console script that tails files, runs each line through FixParser into record_parse_result(), and emits heartbeats. Explicitly not the production entrypoint — that is M1.5 pipeline wiring, and main.py is untouched.

nodes.label: heartbeat: interval config
nodes.rationale: 10s default per FR-HLT-001; emitted even when the agent is idle.

nodes.label: Heartbeat thread/async model
nodes.rationale: run() is a plain asyncio coroutine while tick() is synchronous, and the HTTP sink blocks the loop for at most timeout_seconds (5s). Acceptable for a demo transport because the real Publisher owns buffering and retry (FR-PUB-004/005).

nodes.label: AgentHeartbeat wire contract
nodes.rationale: Exactly spec 004 §6. Extends CamelModel (alias_generator=to_camel, extra='forbid', frozen=True) so the wire is camelCase and Python is snake_case for free and unknown keys are rejected, catching drift. Both agent and backend import the same Pydantic model (FR-ING-022) so schema drift fails at validation, not in production.

nodes.label: AgentStatus literal vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Literal['healthy','degraded','unhealthy'] rather than an Enum, so the JSON stays a plain string with no serializer.

nodes.label: BufferingHeartbeatSink
nodes.rationale: Bounded oldest-first retry queue whose len() is the queue-depth provider, so UBS-60 can be exercised end to end today. It borrows FR-PUB-004's shape (oldest-first, drop-oldest) but none of its sizing or backoff; the real Publisher replaces it.

nodes.label: HealthReporter.build_heartbeat()
nodes.rationale: snapshot() -> derive_status() -> fill the spec 004 §6 model; the only place that knows both the internal signals and the wire model. uptimeSeconds comes from started_at via the injected clock.

nodes.label: derive_status() status rollup
nodes.rationale: One documented FR-HLT-002 rule set instead of per-signal flags, because the spec says status is computed and not hand-set. Any unhealthy reason wins over any degraded one, None signals are skipped rather than treated as 0, and ALL contributing reasons are returned so an operator sees the whole picture.

nodes.label: FileReadHealth per-file entry
nodes.rationale: state is derived, not guessed: 'reading' once a line has been read, else 'waiting'. rotationsDetected stays 0 because LogMonitor does not expose it yet — a documented gap, not a measured zero.

nodes.label: HealthSignals sampled instant
nodes.rationale: Frozen dataclass separating sampling from judging, so derive_status() is a pure function of it and every rule is unit-testable without files, clocks, or parsers. All fields default to None.

nodes.label: heartbeat_json() serialisation helper
nodes.rationale: model_dump_json(by_alias=True), optionally flattened to UBS-66's ingestion contract, in one function so every sink and test serialise identically. Since 2026-09-22 the HTTP sink defaults to wire='ingestion', which drops statusReasons and turns unmeasured signals into 0.

nodes.label: scripts/heartbeat_receiver_stub.py placeholder receiver
nodes.rationale: Not part of the product. A stdlib http.server that validates every POST against AgentHeartbeat (400 with the pydantic error on drift), tracks {agentId: lastHeartbeatUtc, status}, and prints STALE after --stale-after seconds. It exists because UBS-66/87/69 do not, is deleted when they land, and its output shape is explicitly NOT the UBS-69 contract.

nodes.label: HeartbeatSink callable seam
nodes.rationale: Callable[[AgentHeartbeat], None] is the smallest seam between reporter and transport, so the real Backend Publisher (M4) plugs in later without touching the emitter.

nodes.label: HttpHeartbeatSink
nodes.rationale: POST /telemetry/heartbeat (spec 007 §2.3) using stdlib urllib for zero new dependencies. It raises on non-2xx rather than returning False, which is what lets tick() count a failure and lets BufferingHeartbeatSink keep the item queued.

nodes.label: LogMonitor.get_status()
nodes.rationale: Returns FileReadStatus(path, offset, size, last_read_at, read_lag_ms). Takes `now` as a parameter so tests control time without sleeping — a pattern reused by every later method. Offset falls back to the OffsetTracker when no harvester is live.

nodes.label: overall_read_lag_ms()
nodes.rationale: max() of known lags because the worst case is the operator-relevant number; unread files are excluded rather than counted as 0 lag.

nodes.label: Publish queue depth signal (UBS-60)
nodes.rationale: Depth is the leading indicator of a Publisher that cannot keep up; dropped batches are the lagging one. Watermarks use >= because a watermark is a level you reach: 10 is spec 011 §1.1's '< 10 healthy', while 100 is a placeholder with no spec basis, flagged for team review.

nodes.label: queue_depth_provider seam
nodes.rationale: The Publisher (M4) does not exist, so a Callable[[], int] the reporter asks at each snapshot is the smallest possible seam: when the Publisher lands it registers lambda: len(self.queue) and nothing else changes. Until then publishQueueDepth is null, never 0.

nodes.label: Queue depth trend (rising/draining/flat)
nodes.rationale: Spec 004 §6 has no trend field, so putting it on the wire would be a schema change. It is computed from the previous sample (None on the first) and written into the reason text instead; the backend can derive the same from consecutive heartbeats.

nodes.label: Per-file read lag (UBS-30)
nodes.rationale: A file growing but not being read is the most dangerous silent failure: metrics look like 'no activity' while trades happen. last_read_at starts as None (not epoch 0) so 'never read' is distinguishable from 'read just now' (FR-HLT-004). Jira said bytes; specs 002/004/011 say time, so it was built to time (log_read_lag_ms). Threshold comparison is strict >, and an unread file is never flagged because it has no signal either way.

nodes.label: HealthReporter.snapshot()
nodes.rationale: Single place that talks to monitors, windows and the queue provider so everything downstream is pure. Nothing pushes into the reporter except parse results; file status and queue depth are pull-style lookups.

nodes.label: models.ingestion.Heartbeat (UBS-66)
nodes.rationale: UBS-66's independently written implementation of the same spec 004 §6 heartbeat. Requires unmeasured signals as int ge=0, has no statusReasons field while being extra='forbid', types uptimeSeconds as int, and requires resourceUsage and files[].instanceId.

nodes.label: health/wire.py to_ingestion_heartbeat()
nodes.rationale: Flattens the agent's heartbeat to UBS-66's ingestion contract at the sink boundary so the adaptation is isolated to one reversible function rather than spread through the reporter.

nodes.label: Heartbeat document (§6)
nodes.rationale: The canonical heartbeat shape: identity, uptimeSeconds, status, files[] with per-file offset/readLagMs/lastLineAtUtc/rotationsDetected/state, the ...Last5Min signals, publishQueueDepth/publishBufferBytes, activeAlertCount and resourceUsage. FR-HLT-002: status is healthy|degraded|unhealthy DERIVED from a documented rule set in spec 011 §2 rather than hand-set per condition.

nodes.label: AgentHeartbeatMissing (FR-RUL-030, backend-owned)
nodes.rationale: The one rule the backend owns, raised when no heartbeat arrives from a known agent for missingHeartbeatThreshold (default 60s), because a dead agent cannot alert on itself.

nodes.label: health: threshold config block
nodes.rationale: Every FR-HLT-002 threshold in one place: readLagDegraded 5s, parse error rate degraded/unhealthy, rollingWindow 5m backing the ...Last5Min fields, publish queue high/critical watermarks, callback failures degraded.

nodes.label: UBS-58/59/60 implementation notes
nodes.rationale: Working notes for the stacked heartbeat branches: the code says what, this says why.

nodes.label: FR-HLT-004: null means no producer, 0 means measured zero
nodes.norm_label: fr-hlt-004: null means no producer, 0 means measured zero
nodes.rationale: Every signal field is X | None = None. An agent nobody wired a parser into must not claim a clean parse record, so all three parse fields stay None until a producer calls in once (_parse_signal_seen). A gap must never look like a zero.

nodes.label: Spec wins over ticket where they conflict
nodes.norm_label: spec wins over ticket where they conflict
nodes.rationale: Same policy as UBS-30's log_read_lag_ms call. Concretely: interval built at 10s not the ticket's 30s; payload built to the full spec 004 §6 document not the ticket's three fields; status as one documented derive_status() rule set rather than per-signal degraded flags; and the two backend-side ACs (lastHeartbeatUtc, unresponsive) moved to UBS-69 because stale detection must be backend-side. Each needs team sign-off and a Jira amendment.

nodes.label: Windows newline translation broke offset assertions
nodes.norm_label: windows newline translation broke offset assertions
nodes.rationale:
Test write_text/open(..., 'a') calls now pass newline='

nodes.label: Wire compatibility decision: the agent adapts
nodes.norm_label: wire compatibility decision: the agent adapts
nodes.rationale: Two independent models implement spec 004 §6 and only one shape can be on the wire while downstream consumers wait on a working POST /telemetry/heartbeat; verified that our own shape returns 400 and the adapted shape 202. AgentHeartbeat stays the agent's internal truth (keeping its Nones so no status rule fires on a fabricated zero) and wire.py flattens at the last moment inside the sink. Costs, and the reasons to revisit: statusReasons is dropped so the backend cannot answer 'degraded why' and operators must read agent logs (the biggest loss, since FR-HLT-003 exists precisely to avoid guessing); unmeasured signals arrive as 0, the exact misreading FR-HLT-004 forbids; and resourceUsage is fabricated as zeros so a dashboard would plot 0 MB RSS. Reversal is one argument (wire='health') or deleting wire.py, and test_wire_compat.py pins every cost so an upstream contract change fails loudly as the signal to reverse.

nodes.label: Agent processing pipeline (monitor to health reporter)
nodes.norm_label: agent processing pipeline (monitor to health reporter)
nodes.rationale: Fixed stage order: log monitor -> parser -> metrics aggregator -> rule engine -> callback dispatcher -> backend publisher -> health reporter.

nodes.label: BackendUnreachable rule
nodes.rationale: Reads the consecutive_publish_failures gauge >= 5, not a window, because FR-PUB-005's exponential backoff spaces failed attempts further apart as the outage drags on, so a windowed publish_failures count measures the retry schedule rather than the outage (spec 005 §1.2, FR-MET-031).

nodes.label: CallbackFailing rule
nodes.rationale: callback_failures > 3 in 5m; counted only after the dispatcher exhausts retries, so transient errors never inflate it. Lets the agent alert that its own alerts are not reaching Magic.

nodes.label: CancelRejectSpike rule
nodes.rationale: cancel_rejects > 20 in 5m, kept separate from order and session rejects so it cannot dilute either.

nodes.label: ClockSkew rule
nodes.rationale: clock_skew_events > 10 in 5m; indicates a drifting host clock rather than a trading problem.

nodes.label: FixSessionDown rule
nodes.rationale: logouts summed with extraCounters heartbeat_timeouts, >= 1 in 1m, critical. heartbeat_timeouts has no producer and defaults to 0, so the rule still works; a timeout is the absence of a message and belongs to the Health Reporter's tick.

nodes.label: HighRejectRate rule
nodes.rationale: rate on the reject_rate indicator, warning@3% / critical@5% over 5m with minSamples 20, for 2m, resolveAfter 5m. Thresholds are client-confirmed.

nodes.label: NoExecutions rule
nodes.rationale: Guarded absence: executions == 0 over 15m only while guardMetric orders_submitted > 0, so a quiet market is not reported as a fault.

nodes.label: PendingOrderTimeout rule
nodes.rationale: Gauge oldest_pending_age_seconds > 30s with no window. 30s has no spec or client number; it is our reasoning from a typical institutional order-ack SLA. Measures time to first response, never time to fill, so a resting limit order is not penalised.

nodes.label: RejectSpike rule
nodes.rationale: Absolute orders_rejected > 50 in 1m, because at high volume a burst of rejects does not move the percentage rule at all.

nodes.label: SeqGapDetected rule
nodes.rationale: seq_gaps > 0 in 1m. Structural: a skipped MsgSeqNum means messages were lost. A backwards sequence is counted separately as a regression because it skipped nothing.

nodes.label: SessionRejects rule
nodes.rationale: session_rejects > 5 in 5m, critical because 35=3 usually means malformed traffic or a FIX version mismatch rather than a trading decision.

nodes.label: HeartbeatConfig / HealthThresholds / load_health_config
nodes.rationale: Interval defaults to 10s per spec 010 / FR-HLT-001, not the ticket's 30s — spec wins. Frozen dataclasses so a running agent's identity cannot drift. All FR-HLT-002 thresholds are declared up front on UBS-58 so UBS-59/60 add a signal, not a config shape, and __post_init__ refuses nonsense orderings (degraded >= unhealthy). Mirrors the Rule Engine's config_loader: extra='forbid' on our own sections so a typo is refused at boot, extra='allow' at the top level so other components' sections pass through untouched.

nodes.label: Health Reporter (agent self-diagnosis)
nodes.rationale: If the agent stalls, parses garbage, or cannot reach the backend, every downstream metric is wrong while looking healthy. The reporter turns internal signals into one status plus statusReasons and emits them on a fixed interval even when there is nothing else to say (FR-HLT-001).

nodes.label: AgentCounterSampler (UBS-74)
nodes.rationale: Callback counters have no ParsedMessageEvent behind them and live in a monotonic since-startup registry, so they need ingest_agent_counters plus a delta sampler with baseline/rebaseline handling. That separate write path deliberately does NOT touch _last_event_at, because the agent's own dispatcher retrying is not evidence that Magic is still producing log activity.

nodes.label: rules.config_loader (FR-RUL-008/009)
nodes.rationale: Parses config/rules.yaml into RuleConfigs via a local pydantic model mirroring the file's camelCase shape, never partially applying a broken file. Two deliberate loosenings of FR-RUL-009's literal 'refuse to start': a missing file falls back to DEFAULT_RULES because absence is a valid deployment state rather than malformation, and a malformed file on RELOAD is logged while the last-known-good set keeps serving, because 'refuse to start' governs boot and a live process should not die from an operator's YAML typo.

nodes.label: derive_session_counters (UBS-73)
nodes.rationale: Produces logons/logouts, seq_gaps/seq_gap_messages/seq_regressions and clock_skew_events from a real parsed FIX line, so it rides the existing ingest_counters path with SESSION_DIMS (instance_id, session_id).

nodes.label: consecutive_publish_failures gauge (FR-MET-031)
nodes.rationale: Publish attempts failed in a row since the last successful batch commit; resets to 0 on commit and MUST be null — never 0 — when no Backend Publisher is configured, so an agent that cannot report on publishing is never mistaken for one publishing cleanly. It backs BackendUnreachable; the windowed publish_failures counter remains the cumulative trend measure and is explicitly not what that rule reads.

nodes.label: Protocol and session counters (§4.2)
nodes.rationale: fix_messages_total/by_type, seq_gaps, seq_gap_messages (sum of gap sizes), seq_regressions, logons, logouts, heartbeat_timeouts.

nodes.label: Day-1 default rule set (§1.2, FR-RUL-010)
nodes.rationale: The 14 shipped rules. HighRejectRate, AckLatencyBreach and ParseErrorRate thresholds are client-confirmed; remaining values are provisional pending Q-5. NoLogActivity deliberately uses messages_total (every classified line, admin included) over a 60s/1m window rather than a dedicated log_lines_read counter over 5m, to catch a dead pipeline faster. PendingOrderTimeout evaluates time to a tracked order's FIRST response rather than time-to-fill, so a resting limit order is never penalized.

nodes.label: Rule definition and tiers (§1.1)
nodes.rationale: FR-RUL-002: tiers share one condition shape ordered least->most severe, because two thresholds represent one incident escalating rather than two independently-open alerts; dedup identity is per-rule so a tier change never opens a second alert. FR-RUL-004: `for` and `resolveAfter` both exist to prevent flapping. FR-RUL-005: groupBy defaults to [instanceId], and allowing symbol also requires maxAlertsPerRule so one bad session cannot produce hundreds of alerts. FR-RUL-006: rate and latency rules report insufficient_data below minSamples instead of firing.

nodes.label: The five Day-1 rule kinds (FR-RUL-001)
nodes.rationale: rate, threshold, latency, absence, signature. A new KIND requires a code change and a spec update, while new INSTANCES of a kind are configuration only — which is what keeps rule authoring in YAML.

nodes.label: publish: Backend Publisher config block
nodes.rationale: Commented placeholder for UBS-103/104. Buffer is memory only (64 MiB, FR-PUB-008) and the publish token comes from MAGIC_TELEMETRY_PUBLISH_TOKEN, never from the file.

nodes.label: config/rules.yaml live rule set
nodes.rationale: Live source of the 14 rules, parsed by telemetry_agent.rules.config_loader.load_rules (FR-RUL-008/009). SIGHUP-reloadable without losing alert state; a malformed file is rejected naming the offending rule and the last-known-good set keeps serving. Absent file falls back to rules.defaults.DEFAULT_RULES, which this file transcribes one-for-one.

nodes.label: MA-04 alert-readiness mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps each planned Rule Engine alert to what the snapshot already carries versus what must be built elsewhere, so the Rule Engine needs no shape change once producers land. Consecutive-failure streaks and alert dedup are explicitly the Rule Engine's own state, not a windowed-snapshot concept.

nodes.label: Spec 005 — Rule Engine, Alerting and Callbacks
nodes.norm_label: spec 005 — rule engine, alerting and callbacks
nodes.rationale: Alerting lives in the AGENT, not the backend, so alerts survive a backend outage (NFR-REL-003). The backend receives alert state changes for querying and summarisation but is never in the decision path.

nodes.label: Multi-tier severity rule shape
nodes.rationale: Two conditions differing only in threshold are one rule with ordered least->most severe tiers (FR-RUL-002), not two rules, because they are one incident escalating rather than two open alerts.

nodes.label: heartbeat_timeouts deliberately unproduced
nodes.rationale: A timeout is the ABSENCE of a message, which no per-message derivation can observe, so it belongs to the Health Reporter's periodic tick. FixSessionDown sums it with logouts and defaults a missing counter to 0, so the rule works correctly without it.

nodes.label: Agent-local alerting beats centrally-hosted
nodes.rationale: A centrally-hosted alerting system has a structural blind spot: it cannot tell you that it cannot reach you. Because alerting lives on the agent, the agent can report both that its own callbacks are not reaching Magic and that the backend is unreachable, with nothing lost because batches stay buffered and the alert resolves itself on recovery.

nodes.label: Threshold provenance taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Four honest categories rather than pretending every number is tuned: Client-confirmed (only HighRejectRate, AckLatencyBreach, ParseErrorRate); Structural, where the threshold is 'any occurrence at all' because one such event is already an incident; Provisional (Q-5), our starting value flagged in spec 005 §1.2 as pending client input; and Our reasoning, where no spec or client number existed and the rationale lives in the rule's docstring.

nodes.label: Withdrawal of the windowed BackendUnreachable form
nodes.norm_label: withdrawal of the windowed backendunreachable form
nodes.rationale: The earlier '5 publish_failures within 1m' approximation is withdrawn because it cannot work against a publisher retrying with exponential backoff (FR-PUB-005): each failure pushes the next attempt further out, so a fixed-window count measures the backoff schedule rather than the outage severity. Under default interval 10s / base 1s / factor 2 it yields exactly five failures in the first minute — never the six that '> 5' needs — then decays toward one per minute as backoff saturates, making the metric weakest exactly when the outage was worst. The gauge rises monotonically while unreachable and returns to 0 on the first successful commit.

nodes.label: AckLatencyBreach rule
nodes.rationale: latency p95 of ack_latency_ms, warning@500ms / critical@1000ms over 5m with minSamples 50 — a stricter sample bar than the rate rules' 20 because a percentile is unstable at low counts. Client-confirmed.

nodes.label: ParseErrorRate rule
nodes.rationale: parse_error_rate indicator, warning@1% / critical@25% over 5m. dependsOnLogActivity false on purpose: it must keep evaluating precisely when the log pipeline is what is breaking. Client-confirmed.

nodes.label: is_parse_error() definition
nodes.rationale: A closed-set ParseResult.error (line_truncated, frame errors, internal_error) or a framed message with bad_timestamp / unknown_msg_type; warnings such as body_length_mismatch are not errors. Deliberately the SAME definition as the Metrics Aggregator's parse_errors counter so parseErrorCountLast5Min and parseErrorRate can never disagree about the same line.

nodes.label: MetricsAggregator.snapshot(window, group_by)
nodes.rationale: Projects each metric's label tuple down to the requested group_by, summing counters and bucket-merging histograms. An unknown window or a dim no metric declares raises; a metric that merely does not declare a requested dim is silently absent rather than an error. Counters and histograms are returned on the same row but in separate sub-dicts so a caller wanting only one need not filter the other.

nodes.label: Cardinality caps and __other__ folding
nodes.rationale: max_label_sets (5,000 per metric) and max_series_per_bucket (2,000 total, which binds first in practice) fold the label to __other__ rather than dropping data, counting every fold in cardinality_folded. Both reset on bucket reuse, and an __other__ label always projects to one all-__other__ row so folded overflow stays visible however the query slices it.

nodes.label: derive_counters() message separation
nodes.rationale: Dispatches once on msg_type (then on exec_type for ExecutionReport) and returns only counters that actually fired. messages_total fires on every row. Administrative messages fire no trading counters; unrecognised ones fire unclassified_messages.

nodes.label: BASE_DIMS / REJECT_DIMS declared dimension sets
nodes.rationale: Every metric has a fixed declared dimension set (FR-MET-030) so orders_submitted cannot accidentally acquire a rejectReason label. reject_reason resolves through ReasonNormalizer to a canonical label, 'Other' if unmapped and 'unspecified' if absent.

nodes.label: Instance-wide gauges (pendingOrders, secondsSinceLastEvent)
nodes.rationale: Sourced from small additive read methods on existing classes with no change to their write paths. pendingOrders is approximate because the correlator only flags a resolved entry rather than removing it, so a rejected order still counts as pending until TTL eviction.

nodes.label: Histogram (fixed buckets, merge, percentile)
nodes.rationale: 11 fixed exclusive ranges with count/sum/min/max, moved into telemetry_shared.metrics.histogram so one merge/percentile implementation serves both a single agent's buckets and a backend merge across agents, rather than a second implementation that could quietly drift.

nodes.label: LatencyCorrelator
nodes.rationale: Classifies independently of derive_counters: a response is resolved by the TRACKED order's own origin type, never by the incoming message's type. A duplicate or already-resolved response is a silent no-op and an unmatched response is orphan_responses, never a fake latency. Correlation state lives outside the ring buffer with its own TTL (15m) and hard-cap (100k) eviction, both signalling ttl_evictions/cap_evictions plus unmatched_orders.

nodes.label: MetricsAggregator ring buffer
nodes.rationale: Both producers write into one shared store; bucket_start(ts) = ts // bucket_seconds with ring index % capacity. Bucket reuse and expiry clear silently with no signal. tick() runs at the top of both the write and the read path so a stale bucket is never included either way and decay is not something a caller must remember to trigger.

nodes.label: derive_parser_counters (UBS-18)
nodes.rationale: log_lines_read and parse_errors (dimension reason) are parse_error_rate's denominator and numerator, so they ride ingest_agent_counters too — every line must be counted, including lines that produced no ParsedMessageEvent at all. Only hard failures count: bad_timestamp and unknown_msg_type are soft warnings on a line that parsed, and folding them in would fire the rule on well-formed messages.

nodes.label: Agent self counters (§4.3)
nodes.rationale: The agent measures its own health as first-class telemetry: log_lines_read/bytes, parse_errors by reason, clock_skew_events, dropped_stage_events by stage, publish and callback attempt/failure/retry counters, rotations and truncations detected.

nodes.label: Derived KPIs computed at query time (§4.5)
nodes.norm_label: derived kpis computed at query time (§4.5)
nodes.rationale: FR-QRY-010: rejectRate, fillRate, cancelRate, parseErrorRate are never stored, only computed. Each MUST return null rather than 0 when its denominator is below minSampleSize (default 20), so an idle minute never looks like a 100% reject rate.

nodes.label: Dimensions and cardinality caps (§5)
nodes.rationale: FR-MET-029: caps enforced at the agent with a top-N sketch per bucket, folding overflow into __other__ and incrementing cardinality_folded, with the backend enforcing the same caps defensively (FR-ING-006). FR-MET-030: the permitted dimension set per metric must be declared in ONE shared table generated into both agent and backend so orders_submitted cannot accidentally acquire a rejectReason label; series per instance per bucket capped at maxSeriesPerBucket (2000).

nodes.label: Metric snapshot (§3)
nodes.rationale: FR-MET-024: one snapshot per completed 10s bucket per instance, with counters as DELTAS for that bucket rather than cumulative totals — this makes the backend's merge associative and makes agent restarts harmless. An all-zero series must be omitted (FR-MET-027). Gauges are instantaneous at bucket close and the backend takes the latest, never the sum (FR-MET-028).

nodes.label: Trading counters (§4.1)
nodes.rationale: Order lifecycle counters keyed to FIX message types (35=D/F/G/8/9/3) plus quantity sums and the fills_full/fills_partial split on LeavesQty.

nodes.label: MA-epic known gaps (ExecID dedup, timestamp_source)
nodes.rationale: ExecID de-duplication is absent system-wide so a retransmitted ExecutionReport double-counts, and timestamp_source never reaches MetricRow so a caller cannot tell which clock basis a latency used. Both are design decisions (eviction policy, schema change) rather than test gaps, so neither was made unilaterally. Merge associativity is a hand-picked example rather than the hypothesis property test spec 012 names, and pre-rolled 1m/5m rollups are deferred in favour of the proven bounded indexed range-read over the 10s ring.

nodes.label: No-producer rules read as no-fire
nodes.rationale: Rules whose counters have no producer read as 0/no-fire structurally rather than raising — the same posture MA-04 established for parseErrorRate — so an unwired rule is inert instead of crashing evaluation.

nodes.label: LineJoiner caps the checksum-less failure mode below 25%
nodes.norm_label: linejoiner caps the checksum-less failure mode below 25%
nodes.rationale: The most common parse failure (a FIX line with no checksum) is held by LineJoiner as a possible continuation and only counted once it gives up after four lines, so that mode alone asymptotes just under 25% and can never reach ParseErrorRate's critical tier by itself.

nodes.label: A rate returns null, not 0, below minSamples
nodes.norm_label: a rate returns null, not 0, below minsamples
nodes.rationale: One reject out of one order is not a 100% reject rate and an idle minute is not a perfect one, so below minSamples (default 20) the rate is null rather than a number a rule could fire on.

nodes.label: Fixed histogram boundaries (FR-MET-025/026)
nodes.rationale: Boundaries 1,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,5000,+Inf ms are fixed and shared by agent and backend so histograms merge. Percentiles are interpolated at query time and MUST be reported as approximate, while sum/count/min/max accompany every histogram so averages and extremes remain exact even though percentiles are not.

nodes.label: Failure Degradation Order (queries → freshness → callbacks → alerting)
nodes.norm_label: failure degradation order (queries → freshness → callbacks → alerting)

nodes.label: Magic simulator for development
nodes.rationale: Generates configurable FIX send/receive logs because real Magic log shape is unavailable during development.

nodes.label: Unified Telemetry Intelligence (Magic)
nodes.rationale: SMU FinTech project sponsored by UBS; telemetry intelligence for the Magic trading application, delivered as a monorepo with no frontend.

nodes.label: Identity fields (§1)
nodes.rationale: schemaVersion, agentId, application, instanceId, hostname, agentVersion on every event, snapshot and heartbeat. agentId must match the authenticated identity (FR-ING-002) and the backend rejects unknown major versions.

nodes.label: Callback dispatch requirements (§3.1)
nodes.rationale: HTTPS POST only unless allowInsecureCallback is explicitly set for local dev (FR-CBK-001). Per-attempt delivery id plus an idempotency key of alertId+status+notificationCount so Magic can deduplicate retries (FR-CBK-003). Exponential backoff with jitter, base 1s factor 2 cap 60s maxAttempts 5 (FR-CBK-004). HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + '.' + body with the secret from the environment only and constant-time verification (FR-CBK-005). 408/429/5xx/transport errors retry honouring Retry-After while other 4xx is permanent (FR-CBK-006). Bounded queue and capped inflight so a slow Magic endpoint cannot stall the pipeline (FR-CBK-007/008). Response bodies truncated to 200 chars and scrubbed of anything resembling a token (FR-CBK-009). Callback failure must not prevent the alert reaching the backend — the two paths are independent (FR-CBK-010).

nodes.label: Callback flow (§3.2)
nodes.rationale: On firing, one alert event is enqueued for BOTH the Callback Dispatcher and the Backend Publisher. Retryable failures leave the alert firing; on exhaustion the delivery is marked undelivered, callback.failed is emitted, and the CallbackFailing rule is allowed to fire so the delivery failure itself becomes visible telemetry.

nodes.label: Callback payload and CallbackSink seam (§3.3)
nodes.rationale: FR-CBK-012: any 2xx is success even with an absent or unparseable body, and correlationId is recorded when present but never required. Because the final protocol (HTTPS vs message queue, auth scheme, endpoint path) is open question Q-2, the dispatcher must sit behind a CallbackSink interface with HTTPS as the Day-1 default.

nodes.label: callbacks: Callback Dispatcher config block
nodes.rationale: Placeholder mirroring spec 005 §3: bounded queue, capped inflight, exponential backoff with jitter, dryRun default, HMAC secret from MAGIC_TELEMETRY_CALLBACK_SECRET only.

nodes.label: agent: identity config (id, instanceIds, version)
nodes.rationale: Agent identity is frozen config so a running agent's identity cannot drift mid-process.

nodes.label: Spec 004: Telemetry data model
nodes.rationale: The contract between agent and backend. Any change here is a versioned schemaVersion change and both sides must be updated together.

nodes.label: Day-1 deterministic rules vs Day-2 anomaly detection
nodes.norm_label: day-1 deterministic rules vs day-2 anomaly detection
nodes.rationale: Clear separation is required, and all thresholds/anomaly parameters must be configurable; no UBS-specific production data or thresholds may be invented.

nodes.label: Day-2 PostgreSQL historical telemetry
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL is deferred to Day-2 and only for permitted historical telemetry, behind the same repository abstractions as Redis.

nodes.label: Do not overengineer (development principle)
nodes.rationale: Build the smallest testable implementation supporting the architecture and user stories; large changes follow inspect -> explain -> identify -> implement -> verify -> summarise.

nodes.label: Never persist raw logs or raw FIX payloads
nodes.norm_label: never persist raw logs or raw fix payloads
nodes.rationale: Only derived/sanitised telemetry is persisted (aggregated metrics, alert history, anomaly records, callback delivery state, configuration history, approved structured fields) to avoid storing sensitive trading content.

nodes.label: Redis as Day-1 volatile state store
nodes.norm_label: redis as day-1 volatile state store
nodes.rationale: Redis is the shared volatile state store so Day-1 needs no persistent telemetry storage and backend instances can stay stateless.

nodes.label: Repository/service abstraction over stores
nodes.rationale: Redis must never be called directly from FastAPI route handlers; access goes through repositories/services so the store can change without touching HTTP handlers.

nodes.label: Microsoft Teams as the only user interface
nodes.norm_label: microsoft teams as the only user interface
nodes.rationale: No frontend is built; Teams talks only to Backend APIs and must not query Redis/PostgreSQL directly, keeping one access path to telemetry.

nodes.label: Telemetry Agent (architecture constraint)
nodes.rationale: One Agent per Magic instance, deployed alongside it. Must target <2% host CPU and <500 MB RAM, so only lightweight processing runs close to Magic and dependencies stay minimal; expensive historical anomaly analysis is pushed to the backend.

nodes.label: Telemetry Backend (architecture constraint)
nodes.rationale: Many Agents publish to one logical Backend, so instances must be stateless to allow horizontal scaling; built on FastAPI with shared Pydantic schemas.

nodes.label: Open risks (unknown Magic log shape, unproven footprint)
nodes.norm_label: open risks (unknown magic log shape, unproven footprint)
nodes.rationale: Q-8: the real Magic log shape is the highest technical risk, mitigated by a synthetic corpus per spec 012 §3 until sanitised samples arrive. The Python agent's footprint is unproven at load; ADR 0006's reversal conditions apply.

nodes.label: Schema evolution rules (§7)
nodes.rationale: FR-ING-020: adding an optional field or eventType is minor — the backend must ignore unknown OPTIONAL fields but must reject unknown DIMENSION keys. FR-ING-021: removing/retyping a field or changing histogram boundaries needs schemaVersion +1 with one release accepting both. FR-ING-022: the shared schema must live in packages/telemetry_shared/ as Pydantic models; hand-maintaining duplicate schemas across apps is prohibited.
